title: ACA s. 25 — Default of a party

content.overview: Section 25 specifies the consequences when the claimant or respondent fails to take a required procedural step, including failure to communicate the statement of claim or defence and failure to appear or produce evidence.
content.glance: Section 25 specifies the consequences when the claimant or respondent fails to take a required procedural step, including failure to communicate the statement of claim or defence and failure to appear or produce evidence.
content.study:
Module 1: Claimant default
Failure by the claimant to communicate the statement of claim without sufficient cause permits the tribunal to terminate proceedings as provided by section 25.

Module 2: Respondent default
Failure by the respondent to communicate a defence does not by itself amount to an admission; the tribunal may continue without treating the omission as an admission of allegations.

Module 3: Hearing/evidence default
Failure to appear or produce evidence can permit the tribunal to continue and make the award on the material before it, subject to the Act and procedural fairness.

examples.title: Rule applies
examples.body: A respondent fails to file a defence; the tribunal may continue but cannot treat silence as an automatic admission.

examples.title: Rule fails or changes
examples.body: A claimant fails to communicate the statement of claim without sufficient cause; the statutory consequence may be termination under section 25(a).

hypotheticals.question: Does failure to file a defence equal admission?
hypotheticals.analysis: No. Section 25(b) expressly prevents the tribunal from treating the failure as an admission of the claimant's allegations.

rows.right: Does not by itself amount to admission under section 25(b).

misconceptions.trap: Treating section 25 as self-contained without reading its statutory conditions.
misconceptions.correction: Apply section 25 with the Act's express conditions and connected provisions.
